subject: AWS marketplace: billing lag & entitlement backfill plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@datagrid.ai>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@datagrid.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected billing lag in AWS marketplace metering (DataGrid account)

Hi Alex,

Quick note — we've noticed a ~3-week lag between user activity and what shows up in our AWS SaaS metering statements. That lag caused ~2 large invoices to be delayed and a partial double-charge on our internal side (AWS report + direct invoice). We use the SKU mapping we received during onboarding but it feels like some fulfillment records never reached Marketplace entitlement.

Can Redwood help with:
- reconciling which SKUs were not fulfilled for Oct 2026 (we have line items attached from our internal billing)
- a plan to backfill entitlement for unbilled usage so AWS can bill correctly
- confirmation on credits or adjustments while we sort this operationally

Attached: a sample of our internal invoice lines (PO redacted).

Thanks — this is blocking our finance close.

Elena Park
Head of Cloud Ops, DataGrid Inc
elena.park@datagrid.ai
+1 415-555-0129

Attachment: DataGrid_oct_lines_sample.csv (sample)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@datagrid.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, sam.collins@amazon.com
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing lag in AWS marketplace metering (DataGrid account)

Elena — thanks for flagging. Sorry you're running into this. We want to get this reconciled quickly. High level plan:

1) Technical reconciliation: our infra team will compare Redwood's meter submissions vs. AWS fulfillment receipts and identify missing fulfillment files (Rishi will drive).
2) Backfill & fulfill: if there are unsubmitted entitlements, we'll generate fulfillment files to AWS Marketplace for the affected SKUs and dates.
3) Billing/credits: we'll coordinate with AWS AM to request an accelerated billing run or credit for obvious duplicates where AWS confirms the marketplace flow failed.

Please attach your SKU mapping (the mapping you used on your side) and any purchase order IDs. I've looped in Sam Collins (AWS AM) and Rishi to speed the fulfillment side.

Next steps from our side: Rishi will ask for a few logs and a sample entitlement mapping. I'll also open a HubSpot task and attach the DocuSign/PO link when available.

Onward,

— Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-02T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing lag in AWS marketplace metering (DataGrid account)

Hi all — digging in. A few clarifying items before we prepare a backfill: 

- Can you confirm the exact SKU IDs you're using in your internal usage export? AWS expects the marketplace SKU (e.g. sku-012345) not an internal product code.
- For the date range, confirm if we should backfill usage for 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-31 or only the days with missing entitlements.
- Do you use any rate-limiting or aggregator that could have dropped metering calls (we can parse logs if you share a redacted sample).

Technical approach we propose: 
1) You send the attached entitlement-mapping.xlsx (please include your internal product id -> marketplace SKU mapping).
2) We'll run a reconciliation job that compares: Redwood submission logs, AWS fulfillment receipts, and your usage file. Output is a CSV of missing entitlements and candidate backfill rows.
3) With your sign-off we will submit a fulfillment file to AWS Marketplace (per AWS docs). When submission completes we'll generate a report and push to AWS AM and your procurement.

I've attached a PoC patch that generates the fulfillment payload (metering-backfill-script.patch). This will run inside a controlled sandbox; we'll not submit anything to AWS until DataGrid signs off.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: entitlement-mapping.xlsx, metering-backfill-script.patch

Subject: Request: expedited fulfillment processing & backfill for DataGrid (aws-prod-abc123)

Hi Sam / Marketplace Support,

We are preparing a controlled fulfillment backfill on behalf of our customer DataGrid Inc (aws-prod-abc123). Their finance team observed a backlog of unfulfilled entitlements for October 2026. We would like to request an expedited processing window and guidance on whether AWS can perform an accelerated billing run once fulfillment is accepted.

Context:
- Customer: DataGrid Inc (PO pending, DocuSign link below)
- Redwood submission records indicate ~4,200 missing entitlement rows for 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-31 (preliminary)
- Proposed action: Redwood to submit fulfillment file with historical usage (per AWS SaaS fulfillment API) after DataGrid sign-off

Requested from AWS:
- Confirm acceptance criteria for historical fulfillment CSV (field order, timestamp encoding)
- If accepted, can AWS trigger an out-of-cycle billing for affected accounts OR advise on how charges will flow?
- Any rate limits on bulk backfill submissions we should be aware of?

Links & artifacts:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HUB-987654
- DocuSign PO (DataGrid): https://www.docusign.com/Signing/1234abcd
- AWS Product ID: aws-prod-abc123

Marissa (Partnerships) and Karthik (Marketplace) are cc'd to coordinate contractual/fulfillment handoffs. We'll also attach the finalized entitlement-mapping.xlsx after customer confirms mapping.

Thanks — please advise SLA for responses so we can schedule the backfill.

— Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Attachment planned: PO-DataGrid-12345.pdf (will share after DocuSign completes)

Alex / team — thank you, this plan looks good. Quick notes: 

- We've attached the internal->marketplace SKU mapping you requested and confirmed the October date range.
- The PO is in DocuSign and should finish today; I'll upload the PDF when it completes.
- Regarding credits: we'd like Redwood to coordinate with AWS to request a credit for the double-billed items if AWS confirms the duplicate. If AWS cannot credit, we'll need a passthrough credit from Redwood for the amount attributable to a platform-side failure.

Requested timeline: backfill submission this week (target: 2026-11-05) and initial reconciliation report by 2026-11-08. Please confirm if that works for the Redwood and AWS teams.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Cloud Ops, DataGrid Inc
